title: U3 - The rebuilt console at parity, then default
outcome: Settings are navigable structures rather than one dialog holding eight sections whose element identifiers are all named after profiles. The capability workspace renders for the roles it was written for, having previously rendered for nobody. The owner assignment editor exists, is authorized, and is the interface for the endpoint that had none. The rebuilt application becomes the default page.
notInScope: No new product capability and no change to any interface contract: every call the new application makes exists today, and the twelve non-coordinator Domain Capabilities do not become conversational agents. The page that ships today remains in the tree and remains reachable. No visual redesign beyond what the information architecture and the named defects require.
completionEvidence: The contract test covers each restored behaviour and each assertion was watched to fail first. The 231 implementation-pinning assertions in the existing page test are removed in the flip pull request, with the contract test already green for two milestones as their replacement rather than written under pressure alongside the flip. The container comes up and the shipped demo organisation is reachable through it. Reverting the default is a one-line environment change, demonstrated.

metadata.risk: This is the milestone where scope grows, because a settings dialog invites a redesign without end. The boundary is parity plus the named defects, and anything else becomes a new milestone rather than a larger this one. The second risk is a green suite testing nothing: deleting an implementation pin is permitted only where a named contract assertion already covers it.
metadata.migrationRule: The function the router calls keeps its name and gains a selector; the legacy and application renderers are new names, which are safe. The head-request handler reports a length taken from the file on disk and will be wrong the moment the served page is not that file, so it is corrected in the same pull request as the selector.
